title: Trump-backed John James wins Michigan’s GOP primary for governor
summary: Rep. John James has won Michigan’s Republican nomination for governor, NBC News projects.
story: Rep. John James has won Michigan’s Republican nomination for governor, NBC News projects.
James, who represents the Detroit suburbs, prevailed in the primary despite being vastly outspent by his opponent, wealthy businessman Perry Johnson.

President Donald Trump, despite harboring early concerns that a bid for higher office would put the two-term congressman’s competitive House district at risk, endorsed James and last week traveled to the state to campaign for him.

James, 45, will face Michigan Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson, the winner of Tuesday’s Democratic primary, this fall in one of the most fiercely contested battleground states. Term limits prevent Gov. Gretchen Whitmer, a Democrat, from seeking re-election.

An Army veteran who lost two Senate races before winning his House seat in 2022, James presented himself throughout the race as a capable public servant with applicable business experience, given his work with his family’s logistics company.

“This is an amazing state with all the great ingredients, but for the past seven-and-a-half years, under Gretchen Whitmer, we’ve been led to higher taxes, more crime on the roads — and frankly, the roads we have aren’t fixed yet,” James said during a televised debate last month, throwing back to Whitmer’s 2018 campaign vow to “fix the damn roads.”

“We’re going to work together to make sure that our children can read, to make sure that we put criminals in jail, and we hold those accountable who continue to let them back out,” James added. “And we’re going to be making sure that we come together to accomplish the mission of increasing hope and purpose with tested, positive leadership that has actually been tested from the battlefield to business to delivering for you right now.”

Johnson, 78, pounded the state with more than $31 million worth of ads, according to AdImpact, an ad-tracking firm. He drew on his work in quality control and improving business efficiencies while campaigning on a plan to eliminate the state’s income tax. Johnson also drew on his personal wealth, self-funding his run while declining political donations.
“In the state of Michigan, people are really tired of the politicians,” Johnson told NBC News in an interview last month. “I am an outsider. Nobody denies this fact. I’m the outsider of outsiders.”
James’ campaign spent a fraction on advertising — $2.8 million, according to AdImpact.

One potential factor in the results was the absence of former state Attorney General Mike Cox, who dropped out of the primary on July 17 and threw his support to James. Several polls had shown Cox grabbing a substantial share of the Republican vote and raised the possibility of an unpredictable three-way split that could have benefited Johnson.

Meanwhile, the general election challenge eased a bit for Democrats in May when former Detroit Mayor Mike Duggan ended his independent bid for governor. Duggan, a longtime Democrat, had expressed disappointment with both major political parties but caught attention — and grief — from Democrats who noted his reluctance to aggressively criticize Trump.
Michigan voters have not elected a Democrat to succeed a Democrat as governor in more than 65 years.
Benson deputy campaign manager Alyssa Bradley wrote in an email that the secretary of state “begins the general election with something no other candidate can claim: a record of delivering.”
An accompanying campaign memo took a parting shot at both Republican candidates for governor.

“John James and Perry Johnson spent this year lobbing personal attacks at each other and competing for Donald Trump’s attention, not talking to Michigan families about the cost of housing, healthcare, or keeping the lights on,” the memo read. “Both Republican candidates focused on election denying and Donald Trump, while Jocelyn has stayed focused on the issues affecting Michigan families every day.”

title: U.S. airstrikes killed or wounded hundreds of civilians in Yemen last year, sources say
summary: Three U.S. military air strikes in Yemen last year likely killed or wounded roughly 350 civilians, sources told NBC News, but the Pentagon has yet to provide a detailed account  to Congress or the American public.
story: Hundreds of civilians were killed or wounded by U.S. airstrikes in Yemen last year, but the Pentagon has yet to publicly acknowledge the casualties or share a full account with Congress, according to documents reviewed by NBC News and people with knowledge of the attacks.

The three April 2025 strikes occurred during Operation Rough Rider, a 53-day military campaign President Donald Trump launched less than three months into his second term. The stated goal was to stop Iranian-backed Houthi rebels from threatening ships and allies in the region.

Last year, despite detailed reporting from human rights groups on possible large-scale civilian casualties, the Pentagon had assessed there had been no civilian casualties from the U.S. air war against Houthi forces in Yemen.
A Pentagon official said there was nothing to announce at the moment.
“In the coming months, the Department will submit its annual report regarding casualties resulting from United States military operations during the 2025 calendar year,” the official said.

NBC News has reviewed documents showing the back-and-forth between the Pentagon and lawmakers trying to get details on the attacks. In one, the Pentagon wrote to Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., in March, after repeated requests for information about casualties provided no details on the number of casualties, according to one of the documents reviewed by NBC News.

In the letter, the Pentagon’s assistant secretary for special operations and low intensity conflict, Derrick Anderson, said that U.S. Central Command had reviewed dozens of strikes for possible harm to civilians. Fifteen incidents remained under “active review” and three attacks in April 2025 warranted further investigation, with assessments concluding that U.S. strikes “more likely than not resulted in civilian casualties,” Anderson wrote.

Under Trump, the United States has released less information about military operations compared to previous administrations, rarely holding press briefings at the Pentagon. Administration officials have offered few details about damage to U.S. bases or casualties, and in many cases, release  information only after media reports emerge. Officials have rarely acknowledged possible civilian harm from U.S. military operations.

The 2027 National Defense Authorization Act requires that the Pentagon release unredacted civilian harm investigations and all supporting documents for the three strikes in Yemen. Failure to comply allows Congress to withhold some funds, including travel money for Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. There’s no official deadline, but without those details, the Pentagon stands to lose funding.

Lawmakers have repeatedly requested detailed information about U.S. operations in Yemen that may have caused civilian deaths or injuries, but the Pentagon has so far failed to meet their requests, according to congressional aides.

The law also requires the Pentagon to release information about a likely U.S. strike on a school in Minab, Iran, in February, which killed more than 170 people, mostly children. A Central Command investigation into that strike is nearly complete.

During the war with Houthi forces, the U.S. military conducted hundreds of airstrikes, hitting more than 1,000 targets in Yemen, and ultimately reached a ceasefire agreement that included a Houthi pledge to stop targeting American civilian or military ships and a U.S. pledge to stop air and naval strikes in Yemen.

The three attacks occurred on April 17, 2025, at the Ras Isa port in Hodeidah, on April 28, 2025, at the “Ayn Wadi Barracks Warehouses,” and on April 6, 2025, at a private residence, according to Anderson’s letter. But the letter did not offer an estimate of the number of civilian casualties resulting from the strikes or more details about the attacks.

Two people with knowledge of the strikes say that about 150 civilians were likely killed in the first two strikes and roughly 200 wounded. It remained unclear how many civilians were killed in the third strike on the private residence earlier that month.

Human rights groups, citing interviews with witnesses and satellite imagery, previously demanded the U.S. investigate two of the April airstrikes as possible war crimes, saying that dozens of civilians were killed or wounded in the attack at the Ras Isa port and another strike in northwest Yemen.
Amanda Klasing, Amnesty International USA’s national director for government relations, condemned the Trump administration over its handling of the airstrikes.

“The Trump administration’s response has been abysmal. The Pentagon has made no public progress in addressing the airstrike on the Yemeni migrant detention center that killed dozens of civilians, much less taken steps to stop it from happening again.” Klasing said.

“Instead, this administration has gutted the Pentagon’s programs meant to prevent civilian harm and has evaded any public accounting for cases of civilian harm, including the Minab school strike this year in Iran,” Klasing said.

Although Congress in 2019 adopted legislation requiring the Pentagon undertake an array of steps to reduce harm to civilians in military operations, an Inspector General investigation found that the department under Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth slashed funding and cut staff for the effort.

Ras Isa port in Hodeida is a key hub for humanitarian aid shipments with a large civilian workforce, and the April 17 U.S. strike killed or wounded dozens of civilians, according to a Human Rights Watch report last year. The group AirWars, a nonprofit that documents and investigates claims of civilian casualties in war zones, reported that 84 civilians were killed in the strike and 150 wounded.
At the time, U.S. Central Command said the strike was designed to cut off revenue to Houthi forces receiving fuel at the port.
“This strike was not intended to harm the people of Yemen, who rightly want to throw off the yoke of Houthi subjugation and live peacefully,” CENTCOM said in a statement afterward.

The second strike cited in the Pentagon’s letter to Warren referred to a site in northwest Yemen, the same attack that rights groups pointed to in their reporting at the time, according to two people with knowledge of the attacks. A report from Amnesty International said a U.S. strike hit a detention center for migrants on April 28, killing or wounding dozens of civilians. The Pentagon described the target in the April 28 strike as “Ayn Wadi Barracks Warehouses.”

The strike in northwest Yemen was so concerning that, according to Anderson’s letter, U.S. Central Command also conducted a “command-directed” investigation to determine whether any policies were violated or if there was any misconduct by U.S. forces.

The undersecretary of defense for policy, Elbridge Colby, had written to Warren in June 2025 — two months after the three deadly U.S. strikes — saying the Pentagon “has not assessed that civilian casualties have resulted from recent U.S. operations in Yemen since March 15, 2025.”

title: New CDC director is confirmed, giving agency its first permanent leader in a year
summary: The Senate confirmed Dr. Erica Schwartz to lead the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, making her the agency’s first permanent director in more than a year.
story: The Senate on Wednesday confirmed Dr. Erica Schwartz to lead the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, making her the health agency’s first permanent director in roughly a year.

The 51-44 vote was largely split along party lines, with Republicans in favor and Democrats against, though Sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., voted with Republicans. Kaine said last month that he regretted voting against the previous CDC director Susan Monarez and had apologized to her.
Schwartz served as deputy surgeon general during President Donald Trump’s first term; before that, she was a Navy physician and chief medical officer in the Coast Guard.

A series of acting directors have led the CDC since August 2025, when Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. fired Monarez after 29 days in the role. Schwartz takes over from Jay Bhattacharya, who has helmed the agency since February while also directing the National Institutes of Health. Federal law required the Trump administration to nominate a permanent director in March, but Schwartz’s nomination came a month after the deadline.

As CDC director, Schwartz will oversee the country’s public health response, including approving vaccine recommendations and helping contain disease outbreaks. She will inherit a measles crisis — the U.S. has recorded its highest number of cases in 35 years — and a growing outbreak of cyclosporiasis, a parasitic infection that has been linked to shredded iceberg lettuce. Schwartz will also have to contend with rising rates of vaccine hesitancy, which some experts say Kennedy’s rhetoric and policies have exacerbated.

Though Schwartz was widely seen as a conventional pick for CDC director, some public health experts said she didn’t do enough at a Senate hearing last month to distance herself from some of Kennedy’s more controversial stances. Schwartz said at the hearing, for example, that vaccines are safe and effective, but she said she was unaware of some of Kennedy’s vaccine policy changes and dodged questions about whether she supported them.

Sen. Bill Cassidy, R-La., who chairs the Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee and is a doctor, accused Schwartz during her appearance of evading answers to his questions about whether she would challenge Kennedy if he tried to undermine science.
“We need a CDC director that will actually stand up to crazy, stupid things being said that undermine faith in immunization,” Cassidy said.
Cassidy agreed to support Schwartz’s nomination last month, he said, after speaking with her again and talking to those “who served with her and know her well.”
“I am confident that she knows what she is doing and will stand against those who do not,” he said at a HELP committee meeting July 23.

Cassidy added that “as a sign of good faith,” the Department of Health and Human Services recently modified a CDC webpage about vaccines and autism. Since November, the page has claimed that studies haven’t ruled out a link between childhood vaccines and autism, ignoring decades of research that shows no association. That claim has not been removed, but the page now also says that scientists have not identified the root causes of autism.

The National Public Health Coalition, an advocacy group of former CDC employees that has been critical of Kennedy, said in a statement last month that it would not support Schwartz’s nomination based on her performance at the hearing.
“The public needed to hear clear commitments about how she would protect CDC guidance from political pressure. Too often, her stated commitments were incomplete, vague, or missing,” the group said.
Emily Hilliard, an HHS spokesperson, told NBC News last month that Schwartz’s “record speaks for itself.”
“Claiming that Dr. Schwartz was evasive because she declined to speculate on policy decisions outside the scope of her nomination is simply political theater,” she said in a statement.

Kennedy, who has a history of anti-vaccine activism, altered the childhood immunization schedule in January to recommend fewer universal shots to all children. (A federal judge blocked the change in March.) Last year, he fired the members of the CDC’s vaccine advisory panel and replaced them with a group of his choosing, many of whom are skeptical of Covid shots. Monarez testified before Congress last year that Kennedy ousted her for refusing to blindly approve guidance from that panel.
Schwartz said at the hearing last month that Kennedy would never ask her to commit in advance to approve particular vaccine recommendations.
“As CDC director, my sacred responsibility is to provide the American people with public health guidance that is clear, honest and evidence-based,” she said. “I will never betray the science.”

title: Progressives had another big primary night – with a notable exception: From the Politics Desk
summary: Welcome to From the Politics Desk, a daily newsletter that brings you the NBC News Politics team’s latest reporting and analysis from the White House, Capitol Hill and the campaign trail.
story: Welcome to From the Politics Desk, a daily newsletter that brings you the NBC News Politics team’s latest reporting and analysis from the White House, Capitol Hill and the campaign trail.

In today’s edition, we explore one Democratic primary where a progressive challenger was rejected last night. Plus, Andrea Mitchell dives into the clash between President Donald Trump and Jeanine Pirro.
Sign up to receive this newsletter in your inbox every weekday here.
— Adam Wollner
Progressives had another big primary night — with a notable exception
Last night’s primaries brought more success for the progressive wing of the Democratic Party.

Former public health official Abdul El-Sayed defeated Rep. Haley Stevens in Michigan’s high-profile Democratic Senate contest. Activist William Lawrence won the party’s nomination in Michigan’s battleground 7th District. State Rep. Donavan McKinney unseated Rep. Shri Thanedar in the state’s 13th District. And in Kansas’ Democratic gubernatorial primary, state Sen. Cindy Holscher beat state Sen. Ethan Corson, who was backed by outgoing Gov. Laura Kelly.

But that trend notably did not not extend to a key House race in Missouri. In the Democratic primary in the 1st District, Rep. Wesley Bell fended off a challenge from former Rep. Cori Bush in a rematch of their 2024 clash.

As Sahil Kapur and Brennan Leach report from St. Louis, Bush ran on a platform of cutting off U.S. funding for Israel and taking a more combative approach to push Democratic leaders to the left — causes that have powered other successful challengers against incumbents in solidly blue districts.
Still, Bell managed to pull off a 22-point victory thanks to two key factors.

First, Democratic voters broadly saw him as a workhorse who is focused on results and more interested in delivering locally than garnering national headlines. One voter who flipped their support from Bush to Bell over the last two years told Sahil and Brennan that “politics is really complicated, and it’s about the practice and art of compromise.”

Second, he enjoyed a massive financial edge. Bell and his allies — including United Democracy Project, the super PAC aligned with the American Israel Public Affairs Committee — together outspent Bush by a 27-to-1 margin, according to AdImpact.

“There was no secret sauce,” Bell told NBC News when asked how he won his primary while other colleagues have fallen. “There was no shortcut or workaround. It was about getting things done for the people in the St. Louis region.”
Read more →
🗳️ Related: How Abdul El-Sayed won in Michigan — and how the results illustrate his challenges ahead, by Bridget Bowman, Stephen Pettigrew and Makenzie Kerneckel
Trump’s ‘beautification’ campaign becomes his latest loyalty test

With all the other headlines making news in Washington this week — the ongoing Iran war, Abdul El-Sayed’s victory in Michigan, the ethics investigation to Rep. Max Miller — perhaps none is more surprising than President Donald Trump’s fallout with his longtime friend and appointee Jeanine Pirro, the U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia.

What came between the former Fox News host and the president? Something near to his heart, one of his pet “beautification” projects — the renovation of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool — and his stance that his promised cleanup failed because of anti-Trump vandalism.

The president’s focus on the Reflecting Pool is not casual. In May, he drove in his armored limousine right up to its edge to visit the construction and spoke admiringly about the plan to paint the gray stone “American flag blue.” He said it would cost $1.8 million and be finished in a week or two, with no leaks. But within weeks of completion, D.C.’s hot temperatures, interacting with the shallow, still water, produced algae blooms, turning the water green. In mid-June, NBC News photographed Park Service teams pouring hydrogen peroxide into the water and vacuuming the algae. Soon, the admiral blue paint lining the pool began peeling off with large pieces floating on the surface.

Based on Interior Department evidence, Pirro said she charged an Olympian canoeist with a felony for allegedly causing the damage. On Friday, she dropped the charges, blaming it instead on a “botched construction job.” Trump sharply criticized her, angrily saying she had “choked” and “folded like an umbrella.”

That set off a confrontation with one of Trump’s newer allies, Interior Secretary Doug Burgum, whose department has greenlit many of the president’s special projects on National Park Service land around the nation’s capital. In addition to the Reflecting Pool, the Interior Department holds sway over a proposed Trump golf course along the Potomac River, the paving of the White House Rose Garden, and a proposed triumphant arc that would loom over Arlington National Cemetery and the Lincoln Memorial.

NBC News reported that Pirro “had it out” with Trump in the Oval Office on Monday as she defended her decision to drop the case and did not offer her resignation. Trump was still “pretty furious” with her yesterday, one source said, and the president told reporters last night he was still undecided about whether to fire her.

The controversy has been front-page news, highlighting the amount of time Trump spends talking about his D.C. makeover projects, frequently showing visitors and reporters architectural models. It has led to questions about whether this is politically smart when the country is involved in an unpopular war and polls show that voters are much more concerned about the price of gas than beautifying the nation’s capital.

The undersecretary of defense for policy, Elbridge Colby, had written to Warren in June 2025 — two months after the three deadly U.S. strikes — saying the Pentagon “has not assessed that civilian casualties have resulted from recent U.S. operations in Yemen since March 15, 2025.”

title: New CDC director is confirmed, giving agency its first permanent leader in a year
summary: The Senate confirmed Dr. Erica Schwartz to lead the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, making her the agency’s first permanent director in more than a year.
story: The Senate on Wednesday confirmed Dr. Erica Schwartz to lead the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, making her the health agency’s first permanent director in roughly a year.

The 51-44 vote was largely split along party lines, with Republicans in favor and Democrats against, though Sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., voted with Republicans. Kaine said last month that he regretted voting against the previous CDC director Susan Monarez and had apologized to her.
Schwartz served as deputy surgeon general during President Donald Trump’s first term; before that, she was a Navy physician and chief medical officer in the Coast Guard.

A series of acting directors have led the CDC since August 2025, when Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. fired Monarez after 29 days in the role. Schwartz takes over from Jay Bhattacharya, who has helmed the agency since February while also directing the National Institutes of Health. Federal law required the Trump administration to nominate a permanent director in March, but Schwartz’s nomination came a month after the deadline.

As CDC director, Schwartz will oversee the country’s public health response, including approving vaccine recommendations and helping contain disease outbreaks. She will inherit a measles crisis — the U.S. has recorded its highest number of cases in 35 years — and a growing outbreak of cyclosporiasis, a parasitic infection that has been linked to shredded iceberg lettuce. Schwartz will also have to contend with rising rates of vaccine hesitancy, which some experts say Kennedy’s rhetoric and policies have exacerbated.

Though Schwartz was widely seen as a conventional pick for CDC director, some public health experts said she didn’t do enough at a Senate hearing last month to distance herself from some of Kennedy’s more controversial stances. Schwartz said at the hearing, for example, that vaccines are safe and effective, but she said she was unaware of some of Kennedy’s vaccine policy changes and dodged questions about whether she supported them.

Sen. Bill Cassidy, R-La., who chairs the Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee and is a doctor, accused Schwartz during her appearance of evading answers to his questions about whether she would challenge Kennedy if he tried to undermine science.
“We need a CDC director that will actually stand up to crazy, stupid things being said that undermine faith in immunization,” Cassidy said.
Cassidy agreed to support Schwartz’s nomination last month, he said, after speaking with her again and talking to those “who served with her and know her well.”
“I am confident that she knows what she is doing and will stand against those who do not,” he said at a HELP committee meeting July 23.

Cassidy added that “as a sign of good faith,” the Department of Health and Human Services recently modified a CDC webpage about vaccines and autism. Since November, the page has claimed that studies haven’t ruled out a link between childhood vaccines and autism, ignoring decades of research that shows no association. That claim has not been removed, but the page now also says that scientists have not identified the root causes of autism.

The National Public Health Coalition, an advocacy group of former CDC employees that has been critical of Kennedy, said in a statement last month that it would not support Schwartz’s nomination based on her performance at the hearing.
“The public needed to hear clear commitments about how she would protect CDC guidance from political pressure. Too often, her stated commitments were incomplete, vague, or missing,” the group said.
Emily Hilliard, an HHS spokesperson, told NBC News last month that Schwartz’s “record speaks for itself.”
“Claiming that Dr. Schwartz was evasive because she declined to speculate on policy decisions outside the scope of her nomination is simply political theater,” she said in a statement.

Kennedy, who has a history of anti-vaccine activism, altered the childhood immunization schedule in January to recommend fewer universal shots to all children. (A federal judge blocked the change in March.) Last year, he fired the members of the CDC’s vaccine advisory panel and replaced them with a group of his choosing, many of whom are skeptical of Covid shots. Monarez testified before Congress last year that Kennedy ousted her for refusing to blindly approve guidance from that panel.
Schwartz said at the hearing last month that Kennedy would never ask her to commit in advance to approve particular vaccine recommendations.
“As CDC director, my sacred responsibility is to provide the American people with public health guidance that is clear, honest and evidence-based,” she said. “I will never betray the science.”

title: Florida pastor accused of having sex with 14-year-old boy while hiding HIV diagnosis
summary: “Dope-smoking pedophile preacher” Timothy Chaneyfield had sex with an underage boy without telling them he was HIV positive, Florida officials say.
story: A “dope-smoking pedophile preacher” had sex with at least one underage boy and an adult man without telling them he was HIV positive — and Florida officials said Tuesday they fear there might be additional victims.

Timothy Chaneyfield, the 42-year-old pastor at St. James United American Free Will Baptist Church in Winter Haven, was arrested after getting off a plane at Orlando International Airport on July 29, according to a Polk County Sheriff’s Office statement.
The suspect and young male victim, 14, met on a dating app before Chaneyfield allegedly took their chats to Instagram which led to three meetings for sex, the sheriff’s office said.
Tips from Instagram and the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children led detectives to Chaneyfield, Polk County sheriff Grady Judd told reporters on Tuesday.
A 26-year-old man who also had sex with Chaneyfield was located by investigators and tested positive for HIV, Judd said.

“The 26-year-old didn’t know (Chaneyfield was HIV positive) until we brought it to his attention and the 14-year-old had no clue that he was having unprotected sex with an adult that was HIV positive,” Judd said. “This guy’s nasty. He’s a menace to society and he’s proven that.”
Polk County deputies wanted to arrest Chaneyfield last week, but the pastor was in Baltimore, leading a funeral service.
“We actually tried to catch him while he was in Baltimore because we didn’t even want him wandering the streets of Baltimore. What is he up to there?” Judd said.

But the sheriff said his department got “zero assistance” from authorities in Baltimore — an agency, a spokesperson for Judd on Wednesday, identified as the Maryland Department of Transportation Authority police.
A representative for the MDTA police could not be immediately reached for comment on Wednesday.

Chaneyfield has been booked on suspicion of three counts of lewd battery of a minor, three counts interfering with custody of a minor, unlawful use of a two-way communication device, three counts of traveling to meet a minor, four counts of having sex as an HIV-infected person without informing the partner, possession of marijuana and five counts possession of drug paraphernalia.

“This is a dope-smoking preacher right here in front of you,” Judd said. “He’s a dope-smoking pedophile preacher right before you. And now he’s locked up in the county jail where he should be. He was well respected in the community. People trusted him, they believed in him. And now our plea is: if you’ve engaged this guy in sex, let us tell you (about his HIV status) because he didn’t.”
The suspect also worked as the chaplain for Compassionate Care Hospice in Lakeland and had previously been employed by Crystal Lake Middle School as a substitute teacher.
“I would be shocked if there weren’t other children victims out there,” Judd said. “I would be shocked if there weren’t other victims out there. He was very active. He was very engaged.”
Calls to a publicly listed phone number for St. James United American Free Will Baptist Church in Winter Haven on Wednesday were met with a message that the line had been disconnected.
Representatives for Compassionate Care Hospice and Broward County Public Schools could not be immediately reached for comment on Wednesday.

The United American Freewill Baptist Conference said the St. James United American Free Will Baptist Church in Winter Haven “is not affiliated with, governed by, or under the ecclesiastical authority or jurisdiction of the United American Freewill Baptist Conference.”
“Accordingly, we are unable to offer guidance, insight, legal interpretation, or further comment concerning the matter,” the national body said.
It wasn’t clear on Wednesday if Chaneyfield had hired or been assigned a criminal defense to speak on his behalf.

title: 3 people killed, including suspect, in North Carolina shooting
summary: A shooting Wednesday at a home in North Carolina left three people dead, including the suspect, and another person injured, authorities said.
story: A shooting Wednesday at a home in North Carolina left three people dead, including the suspect, and another person injured, authorities said.
Caswell County deputies responded to a call for service just before 8 a.m. at a home on Brooks Road in Prospect Hill, the State Bureau of Investigation said in a news release.
Deputies found multiple gunshot victims. One person was taken to the hospital in an unknown condition.
The identities of the victims and suspect have not been released. Sheriff Tony Durden said at a news conference that everyone involved is an adult and belong to the same family.
Durden said there was no evidence that the family previously reached out to the sheriff’s office.
The Caswell County Sheriff’s Office and the North Carolina State Highway Patrol immediately responded to the shooting, the SBI said in a Facebook post.
SBI crime scene investigators are on scene processing evidence and conducting interviews.
The agency said there is no threat to the general public and that the shooting was contained to the home.
“This was an isolated incident and please keep the family in your prayers,” the sheriff said.
This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

title: Teenager dressed as clown detained in Illinois homicide case
summary: A 15-year-old dressed as a clown was taken into custody Monday night in connection with a homicide investigation in East St.
story: A 15-year-old dressed as a clown was taken into custody Monday night in connection with a homicide investigation in East St. Louis, according to Illinois State Police.

The East St. Louis Police Department received a report of a body in a roadway just after 10 p.m. on Monday and identified the 15-year-old as a suspect after officers arrived at the scene. The teenager, who has not been identified, was detained, though remains unclear whether he has been charged.
The victim was identified as John Wesley Allen Sr., 78, according to the St. Clair County Coroner’s Office. Allen died of multiple stab wounds, the coroner said.
State police acknowledged that “video footage of the suspect dressed in a clown costume has been circulating” and said they are working to obtain all video related to the case.

Doorbell camera footage obtained by NBC affiliate KSDK showed a man with part of his face covered looking into the camera and saying, “I have a gift for you.” Neighbors told the outlet they saw the teenager going door-to-door with a large knife on Monday night.
Corrine Spry was sitting on her back porch with her family when she saw him twirling the knife. She watched him roam the area for about 45 minutes before police arrived.
“He was up to no good,” Spry said. “We’re pretty positive he circled back around in these woods because you could hear the sticks breaking.”
Spry said the suspect could have targeted any neighborhood residents — a thought that still unsettles her, given how easily the situation could have escalated.
Lee Palmer said the suspect approached his mother’s home, where she lives alone, but that she didn’t open the door. Palmer said he hopes the suspect gets help.
“He was not in the right state of mind to walk on somebody’s porch like that,” Palmer said. “It’s just unimaginable.”

Heavy backpacks are all too common, and they can take a toll when students carry them around for eight or more hours at school every day. Carrying a heavy backpack can put a strain on the spine and shoulders, potentially causing short-term effects like soreness and fatigue and long-term bad habits like slouching and poor posture, according to experts I spoke to.

“The back will compensate for any load applied to it for an extended period of time,” says Dr. Jill Noble, the division director of general pediatrics at the University of Michigan Health and Dr. Ingrid Ichesco, a clinical assistant professor of pediatrics at the University of Michigan Health in a joint email response. “There is no evidence that structural spinal deformity can result from backpack use. title: Rep. Chuck Edwards drops re-election bid after censure recommendation over harassment claims
summary: Rep. Chuck Edwards is withdrawing from his re-election campaign in Western North Carolina.
story: WASHINGTON — Rep. Chuck Edwards, R-N.C., said Wednesday he is dropping his bid for re-election, days after the House Ethics Committee recommended he be censured over sexual harassment allegations.

“After much prayer and reflection, I’ve decided to withdraw from my re-election campaign. I will complete my current term,” Edwards announced in a post on X. “Serving Western North Carolina has been the honor of my life. Thank you for your trust, prayers, and support.”
Edwards, 65, had faced mounting pressure over his conduct with two female staffers in his office. He has repeatedly denied wrongdoing.

On Monday, the Ethics panel said it was recommending that the full House censure Edwards after it found that he “engaged in persistent unprofessional and inappropriate conduct towards two young female staffers.” A censure is a formal disapproval by the House.

“The Committee found that Representative Edwards violated the House Code of Official Conduct by failing to adhere to the spirit of rules prohibiting sexual harassment of and unwanted advances to House staffers,” the Ethics Committee said in its 25-page report following a monthslong investigation into allegations against him.
The bipartisan panel said Edwards denied that any of his actions were intended to be sexual or romantic in nature. He cooperated with the investigation, according to the report.

The committee said it found no evidence that Edwards engaged in sexual activity with or propositioned any of his staffers. It also concluded that the allegations “do not implicate quid pro quo sexual harassment” or violate “the ‘letter’ of federal sexual harassment law.”

But the panel added that “his pattern of behavior would lead a reasonable observer to interpret it as such, including providing the young women with lavish and recurrent gifts, making comments regarding their appearance and dress, inviting them to intimate dinners and vacations, sending notes regarding his effusive affection, and inviting them to other activities as a way to spend time together.”
Edwards had been endorsed by President Donald Trump last year and had been set to face Democrat Jamie Ager, a farmer, in the November election.

Democrats believed the seat could flip, given the embarrassing Ethics report and the fact that Ager had significantly outraised Edwards. Before the release of the report, the Cook Political Report rated the race as “Lean Republican.”

State election law allows GOP officials from the counties in North Carolina’s 11th Congressional District to meet and select a new nominee, which the state Republican Party announced they would do next week. The party did not provide timing details.
Edwards has not been in Congress long.

A former state lawmaker, he ousted Rep. Madison Cawthorn in the GOP primary in 2022 but kept a low profile on Capitol Hill, unlike his predecessor, before the ethics probe. Before that, the seat in far western North Carolina was held by Republican Mark Meadows, the former Freedom Caucus chairman who went on to become White House chief of staff during Trump’s first term.

Edwards previously called the allegations “baseless” and said in a statement to NBC News in May that he welcomed an investigation. His counsel wrote a 15-page rebuttal to the committee’s findings, calling them “unfounded.”

summary: The former governor of Virginia is targeting several battleground states with an ad campaign promoting President Donald Trump’s federal school choice program.
story: Former Virginia Gov. Glenn Youngkin, a Republican seen as a potential presidential candidate in 2028, has founded a national policy group that will launch with a push to promote a new school choice program.

Empowering America’s Parents will begin a multimillion-dollar advertising blitz targeting several battleground states, including Arizona, Michigan, Pennsylvania and Wisconsin, a person familiar with the internal planning told NBC News.

The states, led by Democratic governors, are among those that have yet to opt in to the Education Freedom Tax Credit, which was in last year’s One Big Beautiful Bill signed into law by President Donald Trump. The federal initiative is intended to expand school choices for K-12 students and their families.

“Regrettably, 20 states have refused to opt-in to these scholarships,” Youngkin said in a statement announcing the launch of his policy group and an accompanying media campaign. “Empowering America’s Parents will recognize the strong leaders who embraced this program and aggressively call out far-left governors who won’t stand with parents and are instead playing politics.”
Critics have long worried that such programs benefit private schools at the expense of public schools.

Youngkin’s move is likely to intensify speculation that he will seek the Republican nomination for president in 2028. Asked whether the group could be a vehicle for any national political ambitions that Youngkin may harbor and want to hone, the person familiar with the planning noted that Youngkin does not appear in the launch video.
“It’s a great issue for the governor,” this person added. “It’s a great accomplishment for the president.”

The group’s internal polling suggests that people express support for the tax credit once they learn about it but also that awareness of the program is low, the person familiar with the plans said. The campaign will be geared toward persuadable voters, primarily in the suburbs. Empowering America’s Parents also plans to focus on transparency in public education.

“Nothing is more important than our kids, so who’d be against scholarships for tuition, tutoring, services for kids with disabilities, all paid for by a federal tax credit with no state dollars?” a narrator says in the 30-second launch video. “Not hardworking parents — but far-left governors won’t play ball.”

Parents’ rights — particularly in education — became a core issue for Youngkin in his successful 2021 run for governor. He attacked his Democratic opponent, former Gov. Terry McAuliffe, for vetoing bills that would have allowed parents to opt their children out of lessons involving books deemed to have sexually explicit content. (The book at the center of that debate was “Beloved,” Toni Morrison’s Pulitzer Prize-winning novel about the horrors of slavery.)
A unique state law prohibits Virginia governors from serving consecutive terms. Youngkin left office this year, and questions about his White House prospects have followed him.

Vice President JD Vance leads most early polls testing a potential GOP field in 2028, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Sen. Ted Cruz of Texas and Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis among other possible candidates.

title: Man with illegal weapons in home and car is arrested at Trump golf club in California
summary: A man with weapons in his home and vehicle who appeared to be “monitoring security-planning activities” at the Los Angeles-area Trump National Golf Course was arrested days before a planned presidential visit, the county sheriff’s department said Tuesday.
story: LOS ANGELES — A man with weapons in his home and vehicle who appeared to be “monitoring security-planning activities” at the Los Angeles-area Trump National Golf Course was arrested days before a scheduled presidential visit, the county sheriff’s department said Tuesday.
Jeanine John Taele, 38, a resident of the Los Angeles-area city of Downey, was arrested Sunday at the course in Rancho Palos Verdes, the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department said.

The sheriff’s department said deputies found a loaded magazine with hollow-point bullets in Taele’s pants pocket after they’d been contacted by plainclothes federal agents regarding a suspicious person at 3:28 p.m. Sunday.

“The individual was observed walking throughout the golf course grounds taking photographs and videos and appearing to monitor security-planning activities,” the sheriff’s department said in a statement.

In response to the incident, President Donald Trump told Fox News in brief remarks that he took “a little solace” from the fact that such incidents appear to only happen to “consequential presidents.” Adding, “I am definitely consequential.”

The department said deputies arrived and made contact with Taele and learned he was under investigation for robbery in the Los Angeles-area city of El Segundo. They also found a loaded pistol in his vehicle at the club’s parking lot, officials said.
Taele was arrested on suspicion of carrying a concealed firearm and possession of armor-piercing or otherwise prohibited ammunition, the sheriff’s department said.
Taele’s home was searched Monday, and an “illegally modified AR platform rifle,” a .45-caliber pistol, body armor, high-capacity magazines and ammunition were found, the sheriff’s department said.
“Multiple notebooks containing concerning statements” and two “radio signal devices” were also discovered, the sheriff’s department said.

First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bilal A. Essayli said in a statement Tuesday night that Taele has ben charged in a federal criminal complaint with possession of an unregistered short-barreled rifle. The top federal prosecutor for the Los Angeles region said the felony charge carries a minimum sentence of 10 years in prison.

Secret Service agent Armando Marquez, who is in charge at the Los Angeles field office, said in a Wednesday statement that the case “is a strong example of the important work our agents do to keep the individuals we protect and our protected sites safe, starting well before each and every visit.”

“Since the moment our agents became aware of this individual, they’ve worked tirelessly with the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department and our federal partners to investigate this case,” Marquez said.
Taele’s arrest came two days before Trump was scheduled to visit Los Angeles and have a fundraiser at the golf resort. The sheriff’s department did not mention any direct threat to the president.
Trump arrived by Marine One helicopter at the golf resort at around 5:07 p.m. local time Tuesday, according to pool reports.
Taele has been charged in connection with the 2025 robbery, as well as the incident that began Sunday, according to a criminal complaint.

Jail records showed Taele was in custody Tuesday. Online court records did not appear to show an attorney for him Tuesday evening, and efforts to find a phone number connected with him were not immediately successful.

He is charged with second-degree robbery and also three other counts that deal with possessing a large-capacity magazine, having a concealed firearm in a vehicle and possession of a short-barreled rifle, records show.
Rancho Palos Verdes is in the Los Angeles area but is a separate city on the Pacific coast, around 20 miles southwest of downtown Los Angeles.
In 2024, another man, Ryan Routh, was arrested in an assassination attempt on the president at the Trump International Golf Club in West Palm Beach, Florida.

Routh, who the Justice Department said was observed pointing an AK-47 style rifle from a “sniper’s hide” near a fence on the border of the golf course, was convicted in 2025 and sentenced to life in prison in February.

title: Florida pastor accused of having sex with 14-year-old boy while hiding HIV diagnosis
summary: “Dope-smoking pedophile preacher” Timothy Chaneyfield had sex with an underage boy without telling them he was HIV positive, Florida officials say.
story: A “dope-smoking pedophile preacher” had sex with at least one underage boy and an adult man without telling them he was HIV positive — and Florida officials said Tuesday they fear there might be additional victims.

Timothy Chaneyfield, the 42-year-old pastor at St. James United American Free Will Baptist Church in Winter Haven, was arrested after getting off a plane at Orlando International Airport on July 29, according to a Polk County Sheriff’s Office statement.
The suspect and young male victim, 14, met on a dating app before Chaneyfield allegedly took their chats to Instagram which led to three meetings for sex, the sheriff’s office said.
Tips from Instagram and the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children led detectives to Chaneyfield, Polk County sheriff Grady Judd told reporters on Tuesday.
A 26-year-old man who also had sex with Chaneyfield was located by investigators and tested positive for HIV, Judd said.

“The 26-year-old didn’t know (Chaneyfield was HIV positive) until we brought it to his attention and the 14-year-old had no clue that he was having unprotected sex with an adult that was HIV positive,” Judd said. “This guy’s nasty. He’s a menace to society and he’s proven that.”
Polk County deputies wanted to arrest Chaneyfield last week, but the pastor was in Baltimore, leading a funeral service.
“We actually tried to catch him while he was in Baltimore because we didn’t even want him wandering the streets of Baltimore. What is he up to there?” Judd said.

But the sheriff said his department got “zero assistance” from authorities in Baltimore — an agency, a spokesperson for Judd on Wednesday, identified as the Maryland Department of Transportation Authority police.
A representative for the MDTA police could not be immediately reached for comment on Wednesday.

Chaneyfield has been booked on suspicion of three counts of lewd battery of a minor, three counts interfering with custody of a minor, unlawful use of a two-way communication device, three counts of traveling to meet a minor, four counts of having sex as an HIV-infected person without informing the partner, possession of marijuana and five counts possession of drug paraphernalia.

“This is a dope-smoking preacher right here in front of you,” Judd said. “He’s a dope-smoking pedophile preacher right before you. And now he’s locked up in the county jail where he should be. He was well respected in the community. People trusted him, they believed in him. And now our plea is: if you’ve engaged this guy in sex, let us tell you (about his HIV status) because he didn’t.”
The suspect also worked as the chaplain for Compassionate Care Hospice in Lakeland and had previously been employed by Crystal Lake Middle School as a substitute teacher.
“I would be shocked if there weren’t other children victims out there,” Judd said. “I would be shocked if there weren’t other victims out there. He was very active. He was very engaged.”
Calls to a publicly listed phone number for St. James United American Free Will Baptist Church in Winter Haven on Wednesday were met with a message that the line had been disconnected.
Representatives for Compassionate Care Hospice and Broward County Public Schools could not be immediately reached for comment on Wednesday.

The United American Freewill Baptist Conference said the St. James United American Free Will Baptist Church in Winter Haven “is not affiliated with, governed by, or under the ecclesiastical authority or jurisdiction of the United American Freewill Baptist Conference.”
“Accordingly, we are unable to offer guidance, insight, legal interpretation, or further comment concerning the matter,” the national body said.
It wasn’t clear on Wednesday if Chaneyfield had hired or been assigned a criminal defense to speak on his behalf.

title: Third person charged with allegedly threatening witnesses in Nolan Wells investigation
summary: Three people have been charged with allegedly threatening witnesses in the Nolan Wells investigation.
story: Three people have been charged with allegedly threatening witnesses in the investigation surrounding the death of Mississippi teen Nolan Wells in three different instances.
One of the three defendants, Edward James Porter, is accused of making multiple threats to two witnesses July 31, according to court documents obtained by NBC News.

According to a probable cause affidavit, Porter made multiple calls to two witnesses, threatening to kill them and their families. He said he knew where they lived, and told the second witness he would cut them up and put them into a suitcase, the documents said.
Wells was found dead July 6 at the northwest tip of Mississippi’s Horn Island, two days after he ventured to the area with a large group of friends to celebrate the July 4 holiday.

His friends have told officials that they needed to leave the gathering early because their boat was taking on water, and that Wells had told them he wanted to stay behind and catch a later ride with other people. They say that’s when they last saw their friend.
When he never returned home, Wells’ mother and one of his friends reported him missing to the authorities.

The family’s lawyer, civil rights attorney Ben Crump, has since questioned the circumstances surrounding his death — calling into question whether race was a factor, as it appeared Wells was one of a few Black people there that day.
Crump has also rejected notions from law enforcement officials that Wells may have drowned, citing the teenager’s ability to swim well and his athletic past.
NBC News has reached out to Crump for comment.

Officials in Mississippi have also charged Joseph Alfredo Vasquez Dumarce, after he allegedly sent messages on Facebook to a Jackson County Chancery Court judge July 11, according to a probable cause affidavit.
A screenshot of the purported messages included in the court documents shows someone with the username “yaeyae962” threatening to send a bomb to the judge’s office.

“There will be a package coming to your guys office in the next few days. It’s gonna blow you away when you see it lol,” the messages said. “Once that package is opened the timer will start. And then you have maybe 10 seconds or less to ask god forgiveness.”
Authorities then tracked the Facebook account to Dumarce.

The mother of one of Wells’ friends who was with him the day he died, Ashlee Cole, posted on Facebook about the teen’s death and said that her son was cooperating with authorities. Cole is a Jackson County judge, and grand jury charging documents for Dumarce identify the victim in this case as having initials “A.C.”
Cole has since posted screenshots of Instagram and Facebook messages from “yaeyae962” showing the same threatening messages that were included in the court documents.
State completes autopsy of Mississippi teen Nolan Wells

A third person, Michelle Francine Edwards, was charged with making a bomb threat to the George County chancery clerk’s office July 23. Edwards then sent a second bomb threat to the Jackson County sheriff’s office later that day, according to a probable cause affidavit.

Edwards allegedly called the George County chancery clerk more than 20 times in eight minutes July 23 and said “do not go outside,” “the clock is ticking,” and “die,” according to the court documents.
She then called the Jackson County sheriff’s office eight times in a nearly 20-minute period and said, “y’all got a bomb outside, don’t come outside b----,” the probable cause affidavit said.
No attorney was listed as representing Porter, Dumarce or Edwards. NBC News has reached out to the Jackson County public defender’s office for comment on the three cases.

title: 3 people killed, including suspect, in North Carolina shooting
summary: A shooting Wednesday at a home in North Carolina left three people dead, including the suspect, and another person injured, authorities said.
story: A shooting Wednesday at a home in North Carolina left three people dead, including the suspect, and another person injured, authorities said.
Caswell County deputies responded to a call for service just before 8 a.m. at a home on Brooks Road in Prospect Hill, the State Bureau of Investigation said in a news release.
Deputies found multiple gunshot victims. One person was taken to the hospital in an unknown condition.
The identities of the victims and suspect have not been released. Sheriff Tony Durden said at a news conference that everyone involved is an adult and belong to the same family.
Durden said there was no evidence that the family previously reached out to the sheriff’s office.
The Caswell County Sheriff’s Office and the North Carolina State Highway Patrol immediately responded to the shooting, the SBI said in a Facebook post.
SBI crime scene investigators are on scene processing evidence and conducting interviews.
The agency said there is no threat to the general public and that the shooting was contained to the home.
“This was an isolated incident and please keep the family in your prayers,” the sheriff said.
This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

title: Teenager dressed as clown detained in Illinois homicide case
summary: A 15-year-old dressed as a clown was taken into custody Monday night in connection with a homicide investigation in East St.
story: A 15-year-old dressed as a clown was taken into custody Monday night in connection with a homicide investigation in East St. Louis, according to Illinois State Police.

The East St. Louis Police Department received a report of a body in a roadway just after 10 p.m. on Monday and identified the 15-year-old as a suspect after officers arrived at the scene. The teenager, who has not been identified, was detained, though remains unclear whether he has been charged.
The victim was identified as John Wesley Allen Sr., 78, according to the St. Clair County Coroner’s Office. Allen died of multiple stab wounds, the coroner said.
State police acknowledged that “video footage of the suspect dressed in a clown costume has been circulating” and said they are working to obtain all video related to the case.

Doorbell camera footage obtained by NBC affiliate KSDK showed a man with part of his face covered looking into the camera and saying, “I have a gift for you.” Neighbors told the outlet they saw the teenager going door-to-door with a large knife on Monday night.
Corrine Spry was sitting on her back porch with her family when she saw him twirling the knife. She watched him roam the area for about 45 minutes before police arrived.
“He was up to no good,” Spry said. “We’re pretty positive he circled back around in these woods because you could hear the sticks breaking.”
Spry said the suspect could have targeted any neighborhood residents — a thought that still unsettles her, given how easily the situation could have escalated.
Lee Palmer said the suspect approached his mother’s home, where she lives alone, but that she didn’t open the door. Palmer said he hopes the suspect gets help.
“He was not in the right state of mind to walk on somebody’s porch like that,” Palmer said. “It’s just unimaginable.”

title: Perez Hilton’s Family Speaks Out After Reports He Allegedly Livestreamed Self-Harm
summary: Perez Hilton’s family shared a statement after police responded to the celebrity blogger’s home in Miami following a livestream that was flagged in which he allegedly engaged in self-harm.
story: This story discusses self-harm. If you or someone you know is in crisis, call or text 988, or go to 988lifeline.org, to reach the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline. You can also call the network, previously known as the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline, at 800-273-8255, or visit SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources.
Perez Hilton’s family is speaking out after police responded to the celebrity blogger’s home in Miami following a livestream in which he allegedly engaged in self-harm.
Hilton is currently receiving medical care, according to the statement from the blogger’s family and team that was shared Aug. 5 on his website.

The statement comes after reports of “someone who was livestreaming acts of self-harm on social media” the night before, a Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office spokesperson told NBC News. The person was “safely recovered,” the sheriff’s office said. Police did not identify Hilton by name.

“Many of you have reached out with concern for Perez,” said the statement, signed “The Perez Hilton Team and Family.” “We are incredibly grateful for the overwhelming outpouring of love, support, and prayers.”
The family added that their “focus right now is on his well-being.”
“We kindly ask that you respect Perez’s privacy, as well as the privacy of his family, during this difficult time,” the statement said.

The livestream was posted to TikTok before the platform pulled the video. It appeared to show Hilton, covered in blood and holding a knife with signs of injuries. Concerned viewers commented on the livestream, asking for his contact information and offering to call for help.

According to a TikTok U.S. spokesperson, the social media platform’s automated moderator systems flagged the livestream within minutes. Then, the U.S. moderation team reviewed it and law enforcement was alerted.

The content violated the platform’s community guidelines, the spokesperson added. According to TikTok’s mental and behavioral health policies, the platform allows individuals to “discuss emotionally complex topics in a supportive way without increasing the risk of harm.”
“We don’t allow showing, promoting, or sharing plans for suicide or self-harm,” the guidelines say.

Footage from Hilton’s neighborhood, taken by NBC South Florida, showed multiple police vehicles in the area. Cameras from the local NBC affiliate showed paramedics transporting a man into an ambulance and driving away.
The police spokesperson said in a statement that family members of the individual that they recovered have been contacted.
“Deputies quickly located the individual’s residence, where they spoke with family members on scene, and confirmed he was alone inside,” the spokesperson said.

Hilton, who was born Mario Lavandeira, has three children — Mario III, Mia and Mayte Amor— all born via surrogacy. In a 2017 essay published on HuffPost, Hilton also mentioned that his mother lives with the family.
“Not many families are able to have that opportunity,” he wrote in the essay. “That difference makes us special and awesome, to me and us.”
In June, Hilton shared in a video that he and his family had moved back to Miami after a three-and-a-half-year-long stint in Las Vegas.
Hilton’s family and team said in their statement that they plan to share updates “as soon as we can.”
“Thank you for your compassion, understanding, and continued support,” the statement said.
Hilton’s agent Dante Rusciolelli, CEO and talent manager at Golden Arts Entertainment, also shared a statement on Aug. 5, asking the public to honor Hilton’s privacy as he receives care.
“At this time, we do not have any additional confirmed information to share regarding Perez Hilton’s condition,” the statement said.
Verified updates will come “directly from Dante Rusciolelli at Golden Artists Entertainment,” the statement said.

Hilton rose to fame in the early 2000s for his gossip blog, sounding off on celebrity drama. His commentary was often criticized as cyberbullying and labeled as “toxic.” However, Hilton attempted to turn a new leaf years later and embraced a gentler, softer version of himself.

“I’m aware of the fact there are going to be a lot of people with lingering resentment and a lot of skeptics,” he told the New York Times in a 2012 interview. “And that’s OK because I am not pretending to be perfect.”

title: Andy Cohen Politely Reviews Craig’s Attempts at His ‘Real Housewives’ Tagline: ‘Good Starting Point’
summary: TODAY’s Craig Melvin attempted an updated “Real Housewives”-style tagline about himself, and Andy Cohen gave an honest review.
story: TODAY’s Craig Melvin still may not be “Real Housewives” ready.

A hallmark of the 20-year franchise are the taglines cast members say in each show’s intro. Lisa Vanderpump of “Beverly Hills” famously said, “Life isn’t all diamonds and rosé, but it should be,” while “Atlanta’s” Phaedra Parks opted for, “Only God can judge me, and he seems quite impressed.”
In 2022, the TODAY hosts put their own spin on the taglines with “The Real Anchors of TODAY,” which Craig Melvin and Bravo executive producer Andy Cohen revisited in Studio 1A on Aug. 5.
“As a journalist, I usually keep one ear to the ground, because I’m getting the other one pierced,” Craig said at the time, which Cohen gave a “so-so” rating.
Now, Craig’s craving redemption.
“It was mediocre,” he said. “I wanted to try again.”
As the franchise’s unmistakable soundtrack played in the studio, Craig gave it another shot.
“I may spill the tea, but I still keep the glass half full,” he said, a pun on the video podcast he launched in March 2026.
“That’s good ... yes,” Cohen responded.
But Craig wasn’t done.
“Growing up in the South, I was raised to mind my manners, not my business,” he said.
Cohen was less impressed.
“Alright, I’m lost,” Cohen responded with a head shake.
“You’re always honest,” Craig said, before giving it one more go.
“I’m in the business of news, but I’m never above a little drama,” he said.
“That’s a good starting place, we’ll work on that,” Cohen determined.
“I couldn’t be a real housewife,” Craig said with a laugh.
Of the three, Cohen said his favorite was Craig’s first attempt.
“It’s where you’re at on the TODAY show right now,” Cohen said.

Cohen is fittingly looking back at his own television career, celebrating the 20th anniversary of the “Real Housewives” franchise, which he’s led since it launched in 2006 with “The Real Housewives of Orange County.” To mark the milestone, Bravo will release “Real Housewives Ultimate Girls Trip: Roaring 20th,” which premieres Aug. 9.
But Cohen has no intention of slowing down.
“I want to keep this going as long as I can,” Cohen said. “I got kids to feed.”

title: Harry Jowsey Is in the ‘Best Place’ He’s Ever Been After ‘Let’s Marry Harry’
summary: Harry Jowsey speaks to TODAY.com about his new show, Let’s Marry Harry, and why he’s int he best place he’s ever been ahead of the show’s finale.
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Cut for Time,” TODAY.com asks the burning questions our anchors couldn’t get to on-air.

Harry Jowsey has flirted his way across the Netflix dating show universe, from his “Too Hot to Handle” debut to his “Perfect Match” antics. But in his new series, “Let’s Marry Harry,” he’s going all in to find his forever beau.
With “Let’s Marry Harry” production behind him, Harry tells TODAY.com, “It was perfect.”
“I’m in the best place I’ve ever been,” he says.

Across the eight-episode season, the 29-year-old reality dating vet pursues 20 hopeful women, each sporting an engagement ring and vying for his hand in marriage — and the approval of his hand-picked matchmaking squad.

Jowsey’s friends Amanda Kloots, Sonny Henty and ex-girlfriend Georgia Hassarati of “Too Hot to Handle” all pulled strings behind the scenes, making calls like who gets dates, who gets cut and who gets a step closer to the altar. Executive producer and “Call Her Daddy” host Alex Cooper also joined to advise Jowsey as drama reached its boiling point.
Jowsey joined TODAY’s Jenna Bush Hager and Willie Geist to discuss the show on Aug. 5, its premiere date. The final episode premieres Aug. 12.

Discussing his evolution from his reality debut to now, Jowsey said, “I feel like that guy back then didn’t really care too much about anyone else’s feelings. I was a class clown, I was going to do whatever I wanted.”
But for “Let’s Marry Harry,” he joked, he’s “figured out empathy and thoughts.”

After chatting with Jenna and Willie, Jowsey stuck around to break the rest down for TODAY.com: opening up to commitment, dating on and off screen and the self-help steps that got him ready to say “I do.”
This interview has been lightly edited for clarity.

After losing my dad, it was really a pivotal moment in my life. Seeing my sisters with their husbands and kids, and just knowing that I really wish I had that for my dad. Coming back to LA and not having a good support system, I was like, I’ve really got to be serious about love.
I kept asking for a sign, and they kept showing up. It was good.

Leading into it, it didn’t really cross my mind until the first day, and then I was like, “Oh my God, this is really scary.” I think the first fear, or thought throughout, I was just more upset about hurting people because I don’t want to be that guy anymore, and I don’t want to break anyone’s hearts. And obviously, it’s difficult, because that’s kind of a big thing that happens on dating shows. So I think that was my biggest fear going through the whole thing, I don’t want to break someone’s heart.

There was so much different. I was reading a bunch of self-help books, and then Amanda Kloots sat me down for four and a half hours before it, just quizzing everything about my dating life and making sure I was ready. I also knew if I didn’t take it serious and if I was playing around and being a silly sausage, it wouldn’t be good for anyone, and it would really suck. Netflix put all this like money into it and love into it, and I just wanted to make sure I was doing it as best I could.
“He’s Scared, She’s Scared.” It’s this book about self sabotage. I was trying to figure out if I do that a lot, but I think I’m all good now.

All the girls just made it such a safe space. I think I was more upset when they had to hand the rings back. I know a lot of them got quite attached to them. I was just really appreciative because they all were just so warm and made it safe.

I think so. I think dating these days is so difficult, regardless of any of the silly stuff I’ve done. But I feel like it’s helped me become just a way better version of myself because with all those lows, you know you can only come back up, and I’m just grateful I was able to learn from my mistakes.
Yeah, it was perfect. And I’m in the the best place I’ve ever been, so I’m really happy.

I realized I’ve been quite easy to be dismissive and avoidant in the past. Being in an environment like that where you just have to face everything head-on, because if you don’t, then you’re not going to get what you want to show, and also you’re not going to deal with the problem. So it really made me be way better at communicating and also dealing with 20 different personalities at once and learning about that and looking within a lot, which was quite fascinating.
I feel like more now, but leading into the show, I was like, ‘I’m cooked.’ That’s why they had to bring my friends in because I’m spiraling. But yeah, now I trust my thoughts and feelings.

I think I was more nervous for her. It’s such a brave thing to do, and to be like, OK, I’m willing to be a part of this and help an ex when we’ve had quite a colorful past together. I was really grateful that she wanted to do it.
I think “Too Hot to Handle” Harry should have never been in a relationship. He should have just had fun and lived in the moment. I feel like now it’s one person, forever locked in.

title: Will There Be a Season 2 of ‘Sterling Point?’ What Star Ella Rubin Hopes to See
summary: What happens at the end of Prime Video’s “Sterling Point”? Ella Rubin unpacks the twist and shares her Season 2 hopes.
story: In the post-“Summer I Turned Pretty” and “Off Campus” television landscape, “Sterling Point” is the latest to join the ranks of Prime Video teen dramas.

Season 1 of “Sterling Point,” which released Aug. 5, has all the key ingredients: a slow-burn love triangle, beautiful on-location setting, a trendy soundtrack and an ensemble cast of up-and-coming young actors — including leading lady Ella Rubin, who previously supported movies like “The Idea of You” and “Anora.”

“Sterling Point,” created by Megan Park, is an original series that follows city-girl Annie Jacobson after learning she has secret ties to Canada. Annie’s adoptive mother died when she was young, and her father has told her little about her mother’s family.

After her estranged grandfather’s death, Annie heads to his home on Sterling Point, an island off Lake Muskoka in Canada, giving her more questions than answers — at first — and a new outlook on what it means to grow up.
Here’s what to know about the ending of “Sterling Point,” including that plot twist within a plot twist, and what it means for a potential second season.
Warning: Spoilers from “Sterling Point” below.
What Happens in ‘Sterling Point’?
Audiences are right alongside Annie as she uncovers the lies she and her newfound extended family have been told.
After finding letters from her grandfather, previously hidden by her dad, Steven (Jay Duplass), Annie learns about her ties to Canada.

Shortly after arriving in Lake Muskoka, Annie, who was told growing up her parents couldn’t conceive, learns her mother had a biological daughter roughly two years after adopting Annie and her twin brother, Connor.

Ramona was raised by their grandfather in Canada and spent her summers on Sterling Point, which all three siblings will now inherit. Annie and Ramona go from painfully co-existing to forming a deep bond through their separate-but-shared mysterious childhoods.

Together, they learn that Annie and Ramona’s mother grew up coming to the island as a child and had an on-and-off relationship with a man named Joe (Jeffrey Dean Morgan). After adopting Annie and Connor, their mom got pregnant, though her husband Steven was said to be infertile.

It’s revealed she planned to leave Steven, stay on the island to raise Connor, Annie and baby-on-the-way Ramona, and finally be with Joe. She returned to Sterling Point to give birth to Ramona but died in labor because of a previously unknown heart condition.
But after her death, Steven took Annie and Connor back to New York City and concealed their Sterling Point lineage.

The show had one more twist. After learning about her mom and Joe’s affair, Ramona assumed Joe was her father. Then she learns Steven is colorblind, like herself. Because colorblindness is genetic, Ramona makes Steven take a paternity test, revealing he’s also her biological father.
As Annie falls more and more in love with Lake Muskoka, Ramona becomes interested in getting to know Steven.
Where Does the First Season Leave Annie and Ramona?

After a long debate, Annie and Ramona decide to switch places. Annie stays in Sterling Point, and Ramona goes to the city to get a new vantage point. In the final scene, Ramona wake up in Annie’s room in Brooklyn, and Annie in Ramona’s.
“I loved the ‘Parent Trap’-esque ending, and I thought it was that perfect kind of ambiguous, yet satisfying closing loop to the first season,” Rubin tells TODAY.com.
Will There Be a ‘Sterling Point’ Season 2?
Rubin is hoping for a second season to return as Annie.
“Sterling Point” has not been officially renewed for a second season. Park, who wrote and directed the series, has spoken about the possibility of expanding beyond an eight-episode debut.
Rubin shares what she could envision for Annie in the future.

“I don’t know what I can tease, not because it’s a secret, but because there’s so many amazing routes that Annie’s journey can take,” Rubin tells TODAY.com. “I truly don’t know what’s going to happen. And that’s both exciting and nerve-racking because, she feels like someone who’s almost become a sort of friend of mine.
“I don’t know what she’s up to right now, but I hope that she and Ramona are happy with their choices, and also that it leads to some more, you know, fun conflict,” Rubin adds with a laugh.

title: Ella Rubin Channeled These Early 2000s Ballads For Starring Role in Teen Drama ‘Sterling Point’
summary: Ella Rubin unpacks her starring role in Prime Video’s “Sterling Point” and shares how she journaled and listened to music to get into character as Annie.
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Cut for Time,” TODAY.com asks the burning questions our anchors couldn’t get to on-air.

In Prime Video’s new teen drama series, “Sterling Point,” Ella Rubin’s Annie Jacobson leaves the comforts of city life for Lake Muskoka, Canada, and encounters an unexpected reunion with both old and new friends.
The same can be said for Rubin herself, who is making her debut as a leading lady.

Like Annie, Rubin is a born-and-raised New Yorker, and, like Annie, the 24-year-old went to Canada and had an “out-of-body experience,” processing what it means to grow from supporting roles in “Anora,” “The Idea of You” and the “Gossip Girl” reboot into a new phase of her career.

“Sterling Point,” created by Megan Park with executive producers Joshua Schwartz and Stephanie Savage of “Gossip Girl” and the “The O.C.,” is a twisty family mystery with an ensemble of wily, messy teens.

It opens with Rubin’s Annie and her twin brother, played by Keen Ruffalo (son of Mark Ruffalo), learning of their estranged grandfather’s death. His will reveals he left them an island, Sterling Point, located off Canada’s Lake Muskoka. (“Mom was Canadian?” Rubin’s character asks in Episode 1.)

“It kind of unravels her life in this dramatic, funny, beautiful, sad way,” Rubin said of the show while appearing on TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle Aug. 3. “She discovers a lot of secrets that were kept from her, and also a lot of secrets she kind of kept from herself.

“And of course there’s romance and sisterhood and friendship, and it’s really a fun, funny series, but also I think it doesn’t shy away from emotion and tenderness, and it’s a refreshingly tender show,” she adds.

Speaking with TODAY.com after her live interview, Rubin dives into her process finding Annie, unpacks the unscripted moments that made the final cut and pitches why “Sterling Point” stands out among today’s teen drama shows.
This interview has been lightly edited for clarity.

There was a lot more trust, a lot more creative agency. And also just a bigger responsibility in the sense that I wanted to be a good leader in certain ways, and take the responsibilities seriously, of getting to be so lucky to be in a show like this. I just wanted to take it very seriously and kind of take all that I’d learned in the years of doing it here and there and create a fun, healthy, productive environment.

It felt so, so cool. It was really incredible wish fulfillment. They’re just legends, and so I knew I was in really great hands. And then also, five years after doing a job where I was really nervous and unsure, I just felt so lucky to be entrusted in this new way. It was just the coolest out-of-body experience. And also, they’re both really great people.
It just feels really cool to be old enough to have been doing this long enough that I can reunite with someone. It also was a trip in that sense, in the best way.

I think something really special about “Sterling Point” is the grounded-ness, and I think the brilliance of combining Josh and Steph and Megan Park is that there’s a propulsive plot, and it’s a teen drama, and it’s coming of age, but then it also has really real language. It’s very grounded. There’s a lot of genuine emotion. There’s a lot of messiness, and I think we allow the characters to be imperfect, and the show is really, really tender.

Especially with being young women in a show, allowing them to not always be perfectly likable is a really special thing. It explores really intense themes, and it balances dark and light in a beautiful way. There is a lot of grief, and there’s trauma, and then there’s also a lot of friendship and first love and romance and excitement.
Can I tell you something funny about that? That was not planned!

I think something I really, really loved about filming this show is that Megan encouraged constant improvisation, changes, sort of flowing with where the scene took us, which is a really rare gift. When moments like that happen, we just get to fully lean into it and enjoy the kind of spontaneity and ridiculousness of real life, because, like, what’s better than that?
So, essentially, the seaplane took off. That happened, and I just rocked with it and was crossing my fingers that they would use it, because I loved that moment so much.
